title: WPCRL/1560/2016 of Mukim Ahmad minor Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPCRL No. 1560 of 2016
U.C.Dhyani, J.
 Mr. Mohd. Alauddin, Advocate, present for the
writ petitioner.
 Mr. A. S. Gill, learned Deputy A.G., assisted by
Mr. Milind Raj and Mr. Rakesh Kunwar, Brief
Holders, present for the State/respondents no. 1 & 2.
 An FIR has been lodged against the petitioner
being FIR No. 395 of 2016, for the offences
punishable under Sections 377, 506 of IPC and
Section 5/6 of POCSO Act, P.S. Patel Nagar,
District Dehradun.
 After arguing the writ petition at some length,
learned counsel for the petitioner confined his
prayer only to the extent that some time may be
given to the petitioner to surrender before the
Magistrate concerned and, thereafter, court below be
directed to decide the bail application of the
petitioner at an early date.
 Considering the facts of the case, four weeks'
time is granted to the petitioner to surrender before
the Juvenile Justice Board, Dehradun, in as much as
the petitioner says that he is aged 16 years. Learned
counsel for the petitioner has annexed the School
Leaving Certificate to show that the date of birth of
the petitioner is 04.06.2000 and by that analogy the
petitioner is Juvenile. No coercive measures shall be
taken against the petitioner for a period of four
weeks from today.
 If the petitioner surrenders before the juvenile
Justice Board, Dehradun well within time and seeks
bail, it is provided that his bail application shall be
decided at an early date without inordinate delay.
 Writ petition stands disposed of with the
direction as above.
 In the given facts and circumstances of the
present writ petition, this Court does not feel it
necessary to issue notice to the private respondent.
Still, liberty is granted to him to move for recall of
this Order, if he feels aggrieved with the same.
